issue_plan.name: Finish the component evidence foundation
issue_plan.summary: Finish step 1 of #210 with four sequential plumbing changes: repair receipt literals, add separate component evidence records, discover Python components, and show component assurance in the dashboard. Proof, bounded or sampled conformance, runtime checks and declared assumptions stay separate, with no score and no assurance inherited by neighbors. This is the evidence foundation for #210's later execution steps; explicit execution stays guarded by verify.ErrComponents, and TypeScript discovery is outside this plan. Each change keeps SPEC.md and README.md accurate while preserving legacy verification, model-only checking and ratified statements and locks. The merger records the new evidence, assumption, Python identity and display policies; the plumbing builds cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Render explicit receipt literals as code elements
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish the explicit-receipt rendering fix requested by #244. internal/receipt/receipt.go already entity-escapes source-derived text, but statement names, toolchain values, bounds and other literals still pass through backtick spans, where entities display verbatim: No_Double becomes No_Double. Use escaped <code> elements consistently for literals in explicit receipts, including fingerprints, ratified statements, bounds and toolchain values. Escape values before assembling markup, without escaping twice. Preserve original JSON values and legacy Markdown.

Acceptance must check the rendered visible text for underscores, ampersands, angle brackets, backticks, pipes and line endings, including No_Double and toolchain image/tag values. Check that hostile text cannot create HTML, extra table cells/rows, links or forged proof statuses, and retain the existing component-table escaping tests.

Under D-0122 update SPEC.md and README.md for the fix, retaining current execution limits. Correct their remaining-work descriptions to match the narrowed step 1 of #210: #244 supplies the component evidence foundation and views; #210 steps 3 and 4 check unchanged Go and Python packages against a model, and steps 6 and 7 prove selected Go and Python functions in place, each connecting the gate for its own path. TypeScript discovery is outside #210's ordinary Go and Python scope. Decisions: D-0013, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161 and D-0163. Changed SPEC bullets cite their supporting decisions. Keep pinned statements, locks and decisions/ unchanged.

issues.title: Record separate component evidence and all of its inputs
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Extend the explicit component evidence foundation in internal/project, internal/verify and internal/receipt for #244, step 1 of #210. This is an attribution and representation API for supplied results and declarations, extending AttributeComponentProofs; it executes no tools and adds no adapters or gate connection. Keep the existing exact-target proof contract and add independent conformance, runtime-check and trusted-assumption records. Conformance records name the selected driver/check, model, ratified bounds, sampled/bounded-exhaustive mode, observed counts and attempt coverage. Runtime evidence records selected tests and exercised assertions with actual runner outcomes, never inferred target coverage. Trusted assumptions are explicit target declarations with identity, statement, reason/origin and source snapshot, always assumed/unverified. They cannot prove code or satisfy executable checks. This does not introduce production instrumentation or infer assumptions from source.

Extend manifest configuration only as needed for explicit assumption declarations and reproducible check invocation metadata carried as declarative evidence provenance. Executable invocation protocols and runners belong to the later language-specific steps of #210. Inventory/configuration remains intent, never successful evidence. Attribution requires canonical target/check IDs, matching input snapshots, runner/tool identity and actual outcomes. Missing, failed, timed-out, skipped or empty attempts must not yield successful evidence. Reject unknown, duplicate, unselected and stale references atomically. Updating one kind preserves other kinds and the gate outcome; reject changed inventories atomically if retained evidence would have stale snapshots. Proof requires successful exact-target coverage of all selected contracts; neighbors/helpers inherit nothing.

Add separate provenance for selected tests/drivers outside production scope: their files and all actual execution inputs must be hashed without adding them as production coverage rows. Fingerprints bind declarations, selections, model/bounds, all input hashes, evidence/outcomes and tool pins; canonical order, relocation and existing volatile exclusions remain. JSON/Markdown list all components and separate evidence kinds without scores or blanket proof claims. Render text safely and distinguish assumptions from tool evidence, including the footer.

Acceptance uses supplied result records to cover independent evidence on one target, a conformance-only neighbor with no proof, failed/empty attempts, atomic rejection, preservation across attribution calls and rejection of cross-kind stale inventories, full input binding including edits to an outside-scope driver, relocation/order stability, and inert hostile text. Legacy reports and successful legacy fingerprints remain compatible. Keep verify.ErrComponents and the existing refusal before tools start; execution and gate connection remain with the later language-specific steps of #210.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0082, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161 and D-0163. Update SPEC.md and README.md for this shipped evidence API and its execution limit; changed SPEC bullets cite their supporting decisions. The merger records the new evidence and assumption policy because the build cannot write decisions/. Keep ratified statements and locks unchanged.

issues.title: Discover Python components with stable source identities
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Extend project.ResolveComponents and manifest validation to explicit Python scopes for #244, preserving the existing Go and omitted-components legacy paths. Inventory each declared scope directory nonrecursively, including every non-test Python source file, files with no functions, and named functions and qualified methods whether selected or not. Use syntax-aware discovery without importing or executing inspected code. Include async definitions and class-qualified methods; distinguish nested named declarations and repeated definitions rather than silently collapsing them. Comments and strings containing apparent declarations create no components.

Python IDs combine language, project-relative module, qualified symbol and source, with deterministic ordinals where needed. Derive modules from source paths, keeping __init__ files distinct; host import paths, checkout location, line numbers and bodies cannot affect IDs. As in Go, reordering repeated declarations can change which declaration an ordinal selects. Hash complete source files and the exact supported inline Nagini contract bytes independently; ordinary comments and a # +nagini marker alone do not constitute a contract. Document the supported declaration and contract forms.

Resolve target, proof-contract, test and conformance references exactly once, using language-appropriate test files and contract syntax. Keep targets/contracts in scope and permit test/driver associations elsewhere inside the project with the separate input provenance used by component evidence. Reject malformed source, duplicate/ambiguous or missing selections, unsupported selected forms, non-clean paths and paths escaping through symlinks. Inventories remain sorted intent with no assurance. This change supplies discovery, identities, hashes and selection validation only. Keep verify.ErrComponents and the refusal of explicit Python code verification before tools start; never fall through to legacy verification. Execution adapters and gate connection belong to later #210 steps. Explicit TypeScript discovery remains unsupported.

Acceptance covers same-named methods in different classes/modules, async and nested declarations, decorated definitions, duplicate-name handling, fake declarations in strings/comments, function-free files, path containment, invalid references and contracts, and stable IDs after relocation, configuration reordering and body/line edits while hashes change with source or contract bytes. Keep all Go identities unchanged, and check that explicit Python code verification is still refused before tools start while legacy and model-only behavior remain compatible.

Decisions: D-0023, D-0024, D-0031, D-0152, D-0158 and D-0122. Update SPEC.md and README.md to describe Python discovery and its current execution limit. The merger records the Python identity and contract-hashing rules and cites them in the SPEC; this build cannot write decisions/. Keep ratified statements and locks unchanged.

issues.title: Show every component's separate assurance in the dashboard
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish the evidence foundation for #244 by carrying explicit Go and Python component inventory and evidence from receipts through internal/dashboard's snapshot/Project representation into the served UI. Consume the supplied evidence representation established by the preceding issues; this view does not execute checks. Cards and the project table must offer a component view keyed by repository and project, not only by shared model identity: two projects checking the same model can have different component evidence. List every scoped declaration and show its exact identity, source/contract hashes, selected checks and outcomes. Keep proof, bounded or sampled conformance with its actual bounds/counts, recorded runtime-check outcomes, and explicitly unverified trusted assumptions separate. Show unchecked neighbors and failed/timed-out attempts clearly. Do not collapse these facts into one score or promote a partial proof to a project-wide guarantee.

Derive displayed proof and coverage counts from qualifying evidence, including when older reports carry stale top-level labels. Show gate pass/fail independently from successful component evidence; preserve the existing legacy assurance rules and model-only presentation. Cards/table summaries show component evidence and reachable details without blanket proof or unchecked labels. Totals count qualifying proved targets once, excluding contract helpers. Handle empty inventories and absent optional fields safely. Treat all source-derived identities, assumptions and diagnostics as text, with no executable HTML or Markdown injection.

Acceptance checks snapshot/API data and the rendered card, table and detail paths for a mixed receipt built from supplied result records: one proved target, unchecked same-named neighbors, a contract-only helper, successful conformance with no proof, runtime results, a declared assumption, and a failed/timed-out proof alongside a failed gate. Verify two projects sharing one model remain separate, legacy reports retain their claims, empty inventories are handled, malicious strings stay inert and aggregate proof counts agree with target evidence. Exercise the data-to-view behavior, not only source-string presence.

Update SPEC.md and README.md under D-0122 to describe the component evidence representation, Go and Python discovery, and dashboard views delivered by this four-issue plan. Audit all component-related documentation, including the principle and status sections, describing completed capabilities while retaining API-only attribution and the explicit-execution refusal through verify.ErrComponents. Describe #244 as completing step 1's evidence foundation: #210 steps 3 and 4 check unchanged Go and Python packages against a model, and steps 6 and 7 prove selected Go and Python functions in place, each connecting its own gate path. TypeScript discovery is outside this plan. Confirm the retained receipt-literal, separate-evidence, Python-identity and dashboard acceptance, including mixed Go evidence and failed/timed-out proof records, using supplied evidence where execution is unavailable. Keep ratified statements/locks unchanged.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0070, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161, D-0162 and D-0163. Changed SPEC bullets cite their support. The merger records any new display policy; the plumbing build cannot write decisions/. #244 is complete for its parent only when the factory posts completion for this ratified plan's hash.
